{
  "IP": "neorv32_hwspinlock",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Hardware spinlock state",
      "Unit": "neorv32_hwspinlock",
      "Information": "The 32-bit state of the hardware spinlocks, with one lock state per entry, used by software to coordinate mutually exclusive access. It is initialized internally and updated by bus accesses, then returned on lock-status reads.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The state is control/status information rather than inherently secret, although lock_q is returned through bus_rsp_o.data at lines 68-70. A qualifying bus access writes each lock state from not bus_req_i.rw at lines 44-45, so unauthorized activity can alter lock ownership. A write can leave a lock asserted and cause software or the protected operation to wait indefinitely, with the affected state reported at lines 68-70.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker issues qualifying bus reads to set lock bits, or writes to clear them, causing protected software to spin or allowing simultaneous access.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        42,
        45
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        68,
        70
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "Lock entry selection",
      "Unit": "neorv32_hwspinlock",
      "Information": "The selection of which of the 32 hardware-lock entries a bus access addresses, determining which lock is changed or reported. It has no direct entry or exit anchor because bus_req_i.addr only decides the internal select and the selection is not returned as address data.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The addressed entry is integrity-sensitive control information because changing it can steer an access to a different lock; sel is decoded from bus_req_i.addr at line 51 and selects the lock update at lines 44-45 or the returned lock value at line 68.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker changes the access address so an acquire, release, or status read targets a different lock entry than intended.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        51
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus strobe and read/write command",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_hwspinlock",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The bus request record's strobe and read/write fields only describe or trigger an access, so Access command fields bars them as a separate conceptual asset and their effect is covered by the lock state."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus response handshake and error status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_hwspinlock",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The acknowledge only copies bus_req_i.stb at line 63 and the error is tied to a constant at line 64, so handshake-copy and constant-status rules leave no separate security-requiring information."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset control",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_hwspinlock",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The clocks and resets rule excludes clk_i and rstn_i as conceptual assets because they only time or reset the lock and response state at lines 41-43 and 60-62."
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.information: The 32-bit state of the hardware spinlocks, with one lock state per entry, used by software to coordinate mutually exclusive access. It is initialized internally and updated by bus accesses, then returned on lock-status reads.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The state is control/status information rather than inherently secret, although lock_q is returned through bus_rsp_o.data at lines 68-70. A qualifying bus access writes each lock state from not bus_req_i.rw at lines 44-45, so unauthorized activity can alter lock ownership. A write can leave a lock asserted and cause software or the protected operation to wait indefinitely, with the affected state reported at lines 68-70.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker issues qualifying bus reads to set lock bits, or writes to clear them, causing protected software to spin or allowing simultaneous access.

conceptual assets.information: The selection of which of the 32 hardware-lock entries a bus access addresses, determining which lock is changed or reported. It has no direct entry or exit anchor because bus_req_i.addr only decides the internal select and the selection is not returned as address data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The addressed entry is integrity-sensitive control information because changing it can steer an access to a different lock; sel is decoded from bus_req_i.addr at line 51 and selects the lock update at lines 44-45 or the returned lock value at line 68.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker changes the access address so an acquire, release, or status read targets a different lock entry than intended.

considered, not kept.reason: The bus request record's strobe and read/write fields only describe or trigger an access, so Access command fields bars them as a separate conceptual asset and their effect is covered by the lock state.

considered, not kept.concept: Bus response handshake and error status
considered, not kept.reason: The acknowledge only copies bus_req_i.stb at line 63 and the error is tied to a constant at line 64, so handshake-copy and constant-status rules leave no separate security-requiring information.
The clocks and resets rule excludes clk_i and rstn_i as conceptual assets because they only time or reset the lock and response state at lines 41-43 and 60-62.
